title: उपहार कूटनीतिः मोदीले बालेनलाई दिए पिताको पुरानो फोटो
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । उच्चस्तरीय कूटनीतिक भेटवार्तामा उपहार आदानप्रदानको विशेष अर्थ र महत्व हुन्छ । खासगरी राजकीय र औपचारिक भ्रमण गर्दा राष्ट्रप्रमुख वा सरकारप्रमुखबीच उपहार आदानप्रदान गर्ने प्रचलन रहँदै आएको छ । यही प्रचलन धान्दै नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाह आफ्नो पहिलो राजकीय विदेश भ्रमणमा भारत जाँदा भारतीय समकक्षी नरेद्र मोदीसँग उपहार साटासाट गरे । यसपटक भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्रीका तर्फबाट प्रधानमन्त्री बालेनलाई दिइएको एउटा उपहार भने अलि विशेष र चर्चायोग्य रहेको छ । मोदीले बालेनलाई उनका दिवंगत पिता डा. रामनारायण शाहको विद्यार्थी जीवनको पुरानो तस्बिर उपहार दिएका छन् । यो रामनारायणले उच्च शिक्षा हासिल गरेको गुजरातको जामनगरस्थित आयुर्वेद विश्वविद्यालयमा अध्ययन गर्दाको तस्बिर थियो । भारतले बालेनको भ्रमणका लागि कतिसम्म मिहिन तयारी गरेको थियो भन्ने यसले देखाउँछ । बालेनका पिता रामनारायणको गत वर्ष मंसिर १५ गते ७७ वर्षको उमेरमा निधन भएको थियो । पिताको निधनको करिब एक वर्षपछि भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्रीबाट प्राप्त भएको युवावयको तस्बिरले बालेनलाई केहीबेर पक्कै नोस्टाल्जिक बनाएको हुनुपर्छ । बालेनलाई यस्तो उपहार दिएर मोदीले भावनात्मकरूपमा उनलाई पगाल्ने प्रयास गरेको अर्थमा समेत लिइएको छ । त्यसो त बालेन आफैँले पनि भारतमा पढेका हुन् । उनले भारतको कर्नाटकस्थित बैंगलोरमा रहेको निट्टे मिनाक्षी इन्स्टिच्युट अफ टेक्नोलोजीबाट सन् २०१६ देखि २०१८ सम्म स्ट्रक्चरल इन्जिनियरिङमा स्नातकोत्तर (एमटेक) गरेका थिए । तर, बालेनको तस्बिरको साटो पिताको अझै दुर्लभ तस्बिर खोजेर भारतीय कूटनीतिक अधिकारीहरूले उपहारलाई भावनात्मक बनाइदिए । बालेनका पिता रामनारायण शाहको जन्म सन् १९४८ मा महोत्तरीको एकडारा गाउँमा भएको थियो । उनको परिवार खेतीपातीमा संलग्न थियो । उनका पिता मुनीलाल शाह त्यस क्षेत्रका प्रभावशाली जग्गाधनीमध्ये एक थिए । आयुर्वेद चिकित्सालाई आफ्नो पेसा बनाउने निर्णय गरेका रामनारायणले उच्च शिक्षाका लागि भारतको गुजरात रोजेका थिए । उनले जामनगरस्थित गुजरात आयुर्वेद विश्वविद्यालयअन्तर्गतको इन्स्टिच्युट अफ पोस्ट ग्राजुएट टिचिङ एन्ड रिसर्च इन आयुर्वेदमा कायचिकित्सा (आयुर्वेदिक आन्तरिक रोग चिकित्सा) विषयमा एमडी गरे । संस्थानकी निर्देशक डा. तनुजा नेसारीका अनुसार रामनारायणले सन् १९९४ देखि १९९८ सम्म त्यहाँ अध्ययन गरेका थिए । उनी त्यतिबेला नेपाल सरकारका मेडिकल अफिसरका रूपमा कार्यरत थिए । उच्च अध्ययनका लागि भारत पुगेका उनले त्यहाँ चार वर्ष बिताएका थिए । त्यस अवधिमा उनका छोरा बालेन पनि पितालाई भेट्न जामनगर पुगेका थिए । नेसारीका अनुसार बालेनले त्यहाँको विश्वविद्यालयको छात्रावासमा केही दिन बिताएका थिए । अहिले नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री बनेका बालेनको बाल्यकालको एउटा हिस्सा पनि त्यही विश्वविद्यालयसँग जोडिएको रहेछ । मोदीले उपहार दिएको तस्बिर यही शैक्षिक संस्थामा रामनारायणले अध्ययन गर्दाको हो । त्यसो त मोदीले बालेनलाई पिताको तस्बिर मात्रै दिएका थिएनन् । उनले वाराणसीको गंगाजल, बनारसी ब्रोकेड रेशमी शाल तथा रामायणको सम्पूर्ण कथा चित्रण गरिएको कलमकारी चित्रसमेत उपहार दिएका थिए । यता बालेनले मोदीलाई पनि पशुपतिनाथसँग सम्बन्धित रुद्राक्ष, शालिग्राम र चन्दनलगायत सामग्री उपहार दिएका थिए । Kathmandu. Gift-giving has special meaning and importance during high-level diplomatic meetings. It has been a tradition for heads of state or government to exchange gifts, especially during state and official visits. Following this tradition, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah exchanged gifts with his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi during his first state visit to India. This time, one of the gifts given to Prime Minister Balen by the Indian Prime Minister is quite special and noteworthy. Modi gifted Balen an old photo of his late father Dr. Ram Narayan Shah from his student days. This was a photo of Ram Narayan studying at the Ayurveda University in Jamnagar, Gujarat, where he had done his higher education. This shows how much India had prepared for Balen's visit. Balen's father, Ram Narayan, passed away on Mangsir 15 last year at the age of 77. The photo of his youth received from the Indian Prime Minister about a year after his father's death must have made Balen nostalgic for a while. It has also been interpreted as Modi trying to emotionally melt Balen by giving him such a gift. Balen himself studied in India. He did his Master of Science (M.Tech) in Structural Engineering from 2016 to 2018 at the Nitte Meenakshi Institute of Technology in Bangalore, Karnataka, India. However, Indian diplomatic officials made the gift more emotional by finding an even rarer photo of his father instead of Balen's photo. Balen's father, Ram Narayan Shah, was born in 1948 in Ekdara village in Mahottari. His family was involved in farming. His father, Munilal Shah, was one of the influential landowners in the area. Having decided to make Ayurvedic medicine his profession, Ramnarayan chose Gujarat, India for higher education. He did his MD in Kayachitika (Ayurvedic internal medicine) at the Institute of Postgraduate Teaching and Research in Ayurveda under Gujarat Ayurveda University in Jamnagar. According to the institute's director, Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Ramnarayan studied there from 1994 to 1998. He was working as a medical officer for the Nepal government at that time. He had gone to India for higher studies and spent four years there. During that time, his son Balen also reached Jamnagar to meet his father. According to Nesari, Balen spent a few days in the university hostel there. Part of Balen's childhood, who is now the Prime Minister of Nepal, is also connected to that university. The photo gifted by Modi is of Ram Narayan studying at this educational institution. Modi not only gifted Balen a photograph of his father, but also Ganga water from Varanasi, a Banarasi brocade silk shawl, and a calligraphy painting depicting the entire story of the Ramayana. Meanwhile, Balen also gifted Modi with items related to Pashupatinath, including Rudraksha, Shaligram, and sandalwood.

छन् । यो रामनारायणले उच्च शिक्षा हासिल गरेको गुजरातको जामनगरस्थित आयुर्वेद विश्वविद्यालयमा अध्ययन गर्दाको तस्बिर थियो । भारतले बालेनको भ्रमणका लागि कतिसम्म मिहिन तयारी गरेको थियो भन्ने यसले देखाउँछ । बालेनका पिता रामनारायणको गत वर्ष मंसिर १५ गते ७७ वर्षको उमेरमा निधन भएको थियो । पिताको निधनको करिब एक वर्षपछि भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्रीबाट प्राप्त भएको युवावयको तस्बिरले बालेनलाई केहीबेर पक्कै नोस्टाल्जिक बनाएको हुनुपर्छ । बालेनलाई यस्तो उपहार दिएर मोदीले भावनात्मकरूपमा उनलाई पगाल्ने प्रयास गरेको अर्थमा समेत लिइएको छ । त्यसो त बालेन आफैँले पनि भारतमा पढेका हुन् । उनले भारतको कर्नाटकस्थित बैंगलोरमा रहेको निट्टे मिनाक्षी इन्स्टिच्युट अफ टेक्नोलोजीबाट सन् २०१६ देखि २०१८ सम्म स्ट्रक्चरल इन्जिनियरिङमा स्नातकोत्तर (एमटेक) गरेका थिए । तर, बालेनको तस्बिरको साटो पिताको अझै दुर्लभ तस्बिर खोजेर भारतीय कूटनीतिक अधिकारीहरूले उपहारलाई भावनात्मक बनाइदिए । बालेनका पिता रामनारायण शाहको जन्म सन् १९४८ मा महोत्तरीको एकडारा गाउँमा भएको थियो । उनको परिवार खेतीपातीमा संलग्न थियो । उनका पिता मुनीलाल शाह त्यस क्षेत्रका प्रभावशाली जग्गाधनीमध्ये एक थिए । आयुर्वेद चिकित्सालाई आफ्नो पेसा बनाउने निर्णय गरेका रामनारायणले उच्च शिक्षाका लागि भारतको गुजरात रोजेका थिए । उनले जामनगरस्थित गुजरात आयुर्वेद विश्वविद्यालयअन्तर्गतको इन्स्टिच्युट अफ पोस्ट ग्राजुएट टिचिङ एन्ड रिसर्च इन आयुर्वेदमा कायचिकित्सा (आयुर्वेदिक आन्तरिक रोग चिकित्सा) विषयमा एमडी गरे । संस्थानकी निर्देशक डा. तनुजा नेसारीका अनुसार रामनारायणले सन् १९९४ देखि १९९८ सम्म त्यहाँ अध्ययन गरेका थिए । उनी त्यतिबेला नेपाल सरकारका मेडिकल अफिसरका रूपमा कार्यरत थिए । उच्च अध्ययनका लागि भारत पुगेका उनले त्यहाँ चार वर्ष बिताएका थिए । त्यस अवधिमा उनका छोरा बालेन पनि पितालाई भेट्न जामनगर पुगेका थिए । नेसारीका अनुसार बालेनले त्यहाँको विश्वविद्यालयको छात्रावासमा केही दिन बिताएका थिए । अहिले नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री बनेका बालेनको बाल्यकालको एउटा हिस्सा पनि त्यही विश्वविद्यालयसँग जोडिएको रहेछ । मोदीले उपहार दिएको तस्बिर यही शैक्षिक संस्थामा रामनारायणले अध्ययन गर्दाको हो । त्यसो त मोदीले बालेनलाई पिताको तस्बिर मात्रै दिएका थिएनन् । उनले वाराणसीको गंगाजल, बनारसी ब्रोकेड रेशमी शाल तथा रामायणको सम्पूर्ण कथा चित्रण गरिएको कलमकारी चित्रसमेत उपहार दिएका थिए । यता बालेनले मोदीलाई पनि पशुपतिनाथसँग सम्बन्धित रुद्राक्ष, शालिग्राम र चन्दनलगायत सामग्री उपहार दिएका थिए । Kathmandu. Gift-giving has special meaning and importance during high-level diplomatic meetings. It has been a tradition for heads of state or government to exchange gifts, especially during state and official visits. Following this tradition, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah exchanged gifts with his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi during his first state visit to India. This time, one of the gifts given to Prime Minister Balen by the Indian Prime Minister is quite special and noteworthy. Modi gifted Balen an old photo of his late father Dr. Ram Narayan Shah from his student days. This was a photo of Ram Narayan studying at the Ayurveda University in Jamnagar, Gujarat, where he had done his higher education. This shows how much India had prepared for Balen's visit. Balen's father, Ram Narayan, passed away on Mangsir 15 last year at the age of 77. The photo of his youth received from the Indian Prime Minister about a year after his father's death must have made Balen nostalgic for a while. It has also been interpreted as Modi trying to emotionally melt Balen by giving him such a gift. Balen himself studied in India. He did his Master of Science (M.Tech) in Structural Engineering from 2016 to 2018 at the Nitte Meenakshi Institute of Technology in Bangalore, Karnataka, India. However, Indian diplomatic officials made the gift more emotional by finding an even rarer photo of his father instead of Balen's photo. Balen's father, Ram Narayan Shah, was born in 1948 in Ekdara village in Mahottari. His family was involved in farming. His father, Munilal Shah, was one of the influential landowners in the area. Having decided to make Ayurvedic medicine his profession, Ramnarayan chose Gujarat, India for higher education. He did his MD in Kayachitika (Ayurvedic internal medicine) at the Institute of Postgraduate Teaching and Research in Ayurveda under Gujarat Ayurveda University in Jamnagar. According to the institute's director, Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Ramnarayan studied there from 1994 to 1998. He was working as a medical officer for the Nepal government at that time. He had gone to India for higher studies and spent four years there. During that time, his son Balen also reached Jamnagar to meet his father. According to Nesari, Balen spent a few days in the university hostel there. Part of Balen's childhood, who is now the Prime Minister of Nepal, is also connected to that university. The photo gifted by Modi is of Ram Narayan studying at this educational institution. Modi not only gifted Balen a photograph of his father, but also Ganga water from Varanasi, a Banarasi brocade silk shawl, and a calligraphy painting depicting the entire story of the Ramayana. Meanwhile, Balen also gifted Modi with items related to Pashupatinath, including Rudraksha, Shaligram, and sandalwood.

बालेनका पिता रामनारायणको गत वर्ष मंसिर १५ गते ७७ वर्षको उमेरमा निधन भएको थियो । पिताको निधनको करिब एक वर्षपछि भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्रीबाट प्राप्त भएको युवावयको तस्बिरले बालेनलाई केहीबेर पक्कै नोस्टाल्जिक बनाएको हुनुपर्छ । बालेनलाई यस्तो उपहार दिएर मोदीले भावनात्मकरूपमा उनलाई पगाल्ने प्रयास गरेको अर्थमा समेत लिइएको छ । त्यसो त बालेन आफैँले पनि भारतमा पढेका हुन् । उनले भारतको कर्नाटकस्थित बैंगलोरमा रहेको निट्टे मिनाक्षी इन्स्टिच्युट अफ टेक्नोलोजीबाट सन् २०१६ देखि २०१८ सम्म स्ट्रक्चरल इन्जिनियरिङमा स्नातकोत्तर (एमटेक) गरेका थिए । तर, बालेनको तस्बिरको साटो पिताको अझै दुर्लभ तस्बिर खोजेर भारतीय कूटनीतिक अधिकारीहरूले उपहारलाई भावनात्मक बनाइदिए । बालेनका पिता रामनारायण शाहको जन्म सन् १९४८ मा महोत्तरीको एकडारा गाउँमा भएको थियो । उनको परिवार खेतीपातीमा संलग्न थियो । उनका पिता मुनीलाल शाह त्यस क्षेत्रका प्रभावशाली जग्गाधनीमध्ये एक थिए । आयुर्वेद चिकित्सालाई आफ्नो पेसा बनाउने निर्णय गरेका रामनारायणले उच्च शिक्षाका लागि भारतको गुजरात रोजेका थिए । उनले जामनगरस्थित गुजरात आयुर्वेद विश्वविद्यालयअन्तर्गतको इन्स्टिच्युट अफ पोस्ट ग्राजुएट टिचिङ एन्ड रिसर्च इन आयुर्वेदमा कायचिकित्सा (आयुर्वेदिक आन्तरिक रोग चिकित्सा) विषयमा एमडी गरे । संस्थानकी निर्देशक डा. तनुजा नेसारीका अनुसार रामनारायणले सन् १९९४ देखि १९९८ सम्म त्यहाँ अध्ययन गरेका थिए । उनी त्यतिबेला नेपाल सरकारका मेडिकल अफिसरका रूपमा कार्यरत थिए । उच्च अध्ययनका लागि भारत पुगेका उनले त्यहाँ चार वर्ष बिताएका थिए । त्यस अवधिमा उनका छोरा बालेन पनि पितालाई भेट्न जामनगर पुगेका थिए । नेसारीका अनुसार बालेनले त्यहाँको विश्वविद्यालयको छात्रावासमा केही दिन बिताएका थिए । अहिले नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री बनेका बालेनको बाल्यकालको एउटा हिस्सा पनि त्यही विश्वविद्यालयसँग जोडिएको रहेछ । मोदीले उपहार दिएको तस्बिर यही शैक्षिक संस्थामा रामनारायणले अध्ययन गर्दाको हो । त्यसो त मोदीले बालेनलाई पिताको तस्बिर मात्रै दिएका थिएनन् । उनले वाराणसीको गंगाजल, बनारसी ब्रोकेड रेशमी शाल तथा रामायणको सम्पूर्ण कथा चित्रण गरिएको कलमकारी चित्रसमेत उपहार दिएका थिए । यता बालेनले मोदीलाई पनि पशुपतिनाथसँग सम्बन्धित रुद्राक्ष, शालिग्राम र चन्दनलगायत सामग्री उपहार दिएका थिए । Kathmandu. Gift-giving has special meaning and importance during high-level diplomatic meetings. It has been a tradition for heads of state or government to exchange gifts, especially during state and official visits. Following this tradition, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah exchanged gifts with his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi during his first state visit to India. This time, one of the gifts given to Prime Minister Balen by the Indian Prime Minister is quite special and noteworthy. Modi gifted Balen an old photo of his late father Dr. Ram Narayan Shah from his student days. This was a photo of Ram Narayan studying at the Ayurveda University in Jamnagar, Gujarat, where he had done his higher education. This shows how much India had prepared for Balen's visit. Balen's father, Ram Narayan, passed away on Mangsir 15 last year at the age of 77. The photo of his youth received from the Indian Prime Minister about a year after his father's death must have made Balen nostalgic for a while. It has also been interpreted as Modi trying to emotionally melt Balen by giving him such a gift. Balen himself studied in India. He did his Master of Science (M.Tech) in Structural Engineering from 2016 to 2018 at the Nitte Meenakshi Institute of Technology in Bangalore, Karnataka, India. However, Indian diplomatic officials made the gift more emotional by finding an even rarer photo of his father instead of Balen's photo. Balen's father, Ram Narayan Shah, was born in 1948 in Ekdara village in Mahottari. His family was involved in farming. His father, Munilal Shah, was one of the influential landowners in the area. Having decided to make Ayurvedic medicine his profession, Ramnarayan chose Gujarat, India for higher education. He did his MD in Kayachitika (Ayurvedic internal medicine) at the Institute of Postgraduate Teaching and Research in Ayurveda under Gujarat Ayurveda University in Jamnagar. According to the institute's director, Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Ramnarayan studied there from 1994 to 1998. He was working as a medical officer for the Nepal government at that time. He had gone to India for higher studies and spent four years there. During that time, his son Balen also reached Jamnagar to meet his father. According to Nesari, Balen spent a few days in the university hostel there. Part of Balen's childhood, who is now the Prime Minister of Nepal, is also connected to that university. The photo gifted by Modi is of Ram Narayan studying at this educational institution. Modi not only gifted Balen a photograph of his father, but also Ganga water from Varanasi, a Banarasi brocade silk shawl, and a calligraphy painting depicting the entire story of the Ramayana. Meanwhile, Balen also gifted Modi with items related to Pashupatinath, including Rudraksha, Shaligram, and sandalwood.

आयुर्वेद चिकित्सालाई आफ्नो पेसा बनाउने निर्णय गरेका रामनारायणले उच्च शिक्षाका लागि भारतको गुजरात रोजेका थिए । उनले जामनगरस्थित गुजरात आयुर्वेद विश्वविद्यालयअन्तर्गतको इन्स्टिच्युट अफ पोस्ट ग्राजुएट टिचिङ एन्ड रिसर्च इन आयुर्वेदमा कायचिकित्सा (आयुर्वेदिक आन्तरिक रोग चिकित्सा) विषयमा एमडी गरे ।

संस्थानकी निर्देशक डा. तनुजा नेसारीका अनुसार रामनारायणले सन् १९९४ देखि १९९८ सम्म त्यहाँ अध्ययन गरेका थिए । उनी त्यतिबेला नेपाल सरकारका मेडिकल अफिसरका रूपमा कार्यरत थिए । उच्च अध्ययनका लागि भारत पुगेका उनले त्यहाँ चार वर्ष बिताएका थिए ।

त्यस अवधिमा उनका छोरा बालेन पनि पितालाई भेट्न जामनगर पुगेका थिए । नेसारीका अनुसार बालेनले त्यहाँको विश्वविद्यालयको छात्रावासमा केही दिन बिताएका थिए । अहिले नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री बनेका बालेनको बाल्यकालको एउटा हिस्सा पनि त्यही विश्वविद्यालयसँग जोडिएको रहेछ । मोदीले उपहार दिएको तस्बिर यही शैक्षिक संस्थामा रामनारायणले अध्ययन गर्दाको हो ।

त्यसो त मोदीले बालेनलाई पिताको तस्बिर मात्रै दिएका थिएनन् । उनले वाराणसीको गंगाजल, बनारसी ब्रोकेड रेशमी शाल तथा रामायणको सम्पूर्ण कथा चित्रण गरिएको कलमकारी चित्रसमेत उपहार दिएका थिए ।

यता बालेनले मोदीलाई पनि पशुपतिनाथसँग सम्बन्धित रुद्राक्ष, शालिग्राम र चन्दनलगायत सामग्री उपहार दिएका थिए ।

Kathmandu. Gift-giving has special meaning and importance during high-level diplomatic meetings. It has been a tradition for heads of state or government to exchange gifts, especially during state and official visits. Following this tradition, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah exchanged gifts with his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi during his first state visit to India. This time, one of the gifts given to Prime Minister Balen by the Indian Prime Minister is quite special and noteworthy. Modi gifted Balen an old photo of his late father Dr. Ram Narayan Shah from his student days. This was a photo of Ram Narayan studying at the Ayurveda University in Jamnagar, Gujarat, where he had done his higher education. This shows how much India had prepared for Balen's visit. Balen's father, Ram Narayan, passed away on Mangsir 15 last year at the age of 77. The photo of his youth received from the Indian Prime Minister about a year after his father's death must have made Balen nostalgic for a while. It has also been interpreted as Modi trying to emotionally melt Balen by giving him such a gift. Balen himself studied in India. He did his Master of Science (M.Tech) in Structural Engineering from 2016 to 2018 at the Nitte Meenakshi Institute of Technology in Bangalore, Karnataka, India. However, Indian diplomatic officials made the gift more emotional by finding an even rarer photo of his father instead of Balen's photo. Balen's father, Ram Narayan Shah, was born in 1948 in Ekdara village in Mahottari. His family was involved in farming. His father, Munilal Shah, was one of the influential landowners in the area. Having decided to make Ayurvedic medicine his profession, Ramnarayan chose Gujarat, India for higher education. He did his MD in Kayachitika (Ayurvedic internal medicine) at the Institute of Postgraduate Teaching and Research in Ayurveda under Gujarat Ayurveda University in Jamnagar. According to the institute's director, Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Ramnarayan studied there from 1994 to 1998. He was working as a medical officer for the Nepal government at that time. He had gone to India for higher studies and spent four years there. During that time, his son Balen also reached Jamnagar to meet his father. According to Nesari, Balen spent a few days in the university hostel there. Part of Balen's childhood, who is now the Prime Minister of Nepal, is also connected to that university. The photo gifted by Modi is of Ram Narayan studying at this educational institution. Modi not only gifted Balen a photograph of his father, but also Ganga water from Varanasi, a Banarasi brocade silk shawl, and a calligraphy painting depicting the entire story of the Ramayana. Meanwhile, Balen also gifted Modi with items related to Pashupatinath, including Rudraksha, Shaligram, and sandalwood.
